_note: What Haru, the straw weaver of Kaminoda, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction. On the bamboo hill she has her own lines (map condition). The birthday lines (summer 27), the close lines from band 4 and the sandal lines once her band 5 scene is seen (heart_haru_5). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Genzo says he comes for the dango. He comes for the blossoms. Don't tell him I said so.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: All these lanterns! Up in Kaminoda the only lights at night are the fireflies.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I brought a sprig of pampas from our dike for the moon table. It's the tall one.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I wrote my wish for the year on a slip of paper. If I tell you, it won't come true.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Twice in a day! Careful, people will say you've taken a liking to Kaminoda.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I'm mid-braid, so I'll talk with my hands busy. Go on.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Oh! A new face up here. I'm Haru. I weave straw: sandals, mats, rope, whatever's needed.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: If your sandals wear through, come see me before you buy some in the village.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You found my spot. On a clear day you can count every roof in the valley from here.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The bamboo creaks when the wind turns. Grandma said it's the hill talking in its sleep.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Rain's good for straw work: damp straw doesn't snap. My fingers say otherwise.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The eggplants are coming along. I talk to them. Don't laugh, it works.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Morning's for the garden, before the slugs wake up and have their breakfast.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The rack's full of sheaves! The whole lane smells of sun and straw.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Winter's for weaving. Snow boots, straw capes. The whole hamlet walks in my work.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Genzo pretends he doesn't need help with the rack. Then he lets me do all of it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I go up the hill most afternoons. Thinking's easier with the wind in your ears.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: The persimmons in the orchard turn orange in fall. Dried, they're the best thing in winter.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Bamboo shoots poke up where the lane climbs to the hill. And there's wild garlic past the far end of the lower paddies. Genzo says garlic is for the young. He eats it anyway.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Wild raspberries by the pine at the top of the terraces, and more past the far end of the lower paddies. Half of mine never make it home.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Yam bulbils in the persimmon orchard and under the bamboo, tiny as beads. Boiled with rice they're lovely. The chestnuts are past the lower paddies.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Genzo's woodpile grows enoki in winter. He calls them his lodgers and lets them stay rent-free.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You remembered? Then today I weave nothing. I'm going up the hill to sit and count clouds, and nobody can stop me.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A birthday present? For me? Grandma used to give me a new braid of red cord. I'll tie this in my memory next to it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I left a straw hat on your gate post. Summer sun up on the field is no joke. It's the right size, I measured you by eye.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: When I'm on the hill I can see your field from the lookout. A tiny square of brown. I wave sometimes. You never wave back.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Sayo sold three pairs of my sandals this week! Three! I'm going to need more straw than Genzo's paddies can grow.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: I still go up the hill. Not to think about leaving now. Just to look. It's a different view when you've chosen it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: For me? Oh, this is lovely! I'll think of you every time I have one.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Thank you! That's kind of you.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Oh, thanks. I'm sure it'll be useful.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Ah... I'm not one for fish, I'm afraid. The eyes look at me.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A rock? Is this a joke? I have plenty, thank you.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Another one? No, no, one's enough for today. Save it for yourself.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A paper fan! I'll keep it on my workbench. Straw dust and summer heat, beware.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: You made this? It's wonderful. Can you teach me sometime?

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Still warm! I'll eat it on the hill this afternoon.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Oh, a dish. Thank you, I'll have it for supper.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Fish again... You're kind, but I'll pass this to Genzo.
